unsupported: fill other than none (native fills with ff_draw when the colour parses, otherwise silently ignores it)
overlapping layouts: native process_slice copies inputs on parallel slice jobs, so overlapping bytes are racy (measured 7 distinct outputs in 12 default-thread runs, 1 with -filter_complex_threads 1)
layouts leaving bytes uncovered (native output is uninitialised pool memory)
placements whose rounded-up chroma passes a plane's width or height (odd sizes with subsampled chroma; native writes into padding or past the plane)
more than 32 inputs, grid abbreviations or non-'x' separators, and the lenient layout forms native accepts (extra or empty items, extra _ parts, whitespace, trailing text)
enable= (native has no timeline support), runtime commands, and the linear path (join role)

sharedEditsNeeded: tests/helpers/video-negotiation-cases.ts: it always runs a linear chain, which a join cannot; a join-aware mode would let joins share it. This branch keeps its own join form in its differential file, as maskedmerge does.
notes: Spec deviation: the scope says overlaps are kept with later inputs overwriting earlier ones. That matches native only single-threaded (622/622 cases including three overlap layouts with -filter_complex_threads 1); with default threads native overlap output is nondeterministic, so overlaps are refused and [THREADS] holds for every accepted case.

Out-of-plane chroma placements are refused rather than clipped (hstack/vstack clip them): whether native's write lands in invisible padding or in the next row depends on the frame pool's line alignment.
-filter_threads only affects simple filtergraphs; the threads test also passes -filter_complex_threads 1, which is the option that governs -filter_complex.

Native exit statuses: EINVAL cases use 256-os.constants.errno.EINVAL; enable= exits 176 (AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME) and unknown framesync options exit 8 (AVERROR_OPTION_NOT_FOUND), which are not errno values. fill=red, fill=bogus, gaps, overlaps and out-of-plane chroma exit 0 natively and are refused here only.
The sandbox Node was 22.23.5 and bootstrap requires Node 24; the preinstalled /opt/node24 (v24.22.3) was used for everything.
Reference: an unpinned sandbox build (--allow-unpinned-reference); its ffmpeg sha256 differs from the linux-x64 pin; the tests check only the commit and --disable-x86asm.

Setup durations: bootstrap 2m49s (npm 8.0s, submodule 5.5s, reference build 154s); baseline typecheck + lint + boundaries + registry test 51s, all green. The baseline ran while the new kernel file already existed untracked, before the registry line was added.
